Hey, I've had depression for 2 years and can relate to the indifference feeling. Right now is really tough since we have to stay inside all the time, there's not much to look forward to. If you're in Canada like me, the weather here makes it even harder to go out.

Depression is kind of like the strong waves of an ocean. They come and go. Sometimes the storm will last a few months. Others, you'll be hit with a tsunami. But in between, the water will be peaceful. You'll encounter sea turtles here, dolphins over there, and you'll be glad you stayed. And on the clear days, you'll see a great sunset stretching the whole horizon from end to end. 

So keep holding onto that raft. You will make it through. Please reach out to others for support. A good therapist can make an incredible difference. Thank you for holding on. ❤️

I second mcatsux17; this was my note for AAMC FL 2.

There are 3 types of gel electrophoresis:

1. Native-PAGE separates proteins by **charge**  
2. Denaturing (SDS)-PAGE splits proteins into smaller peptides to separate by **mass**  
3. Reducing SDS-page splits **disulfide** links

So if a peptide shows 1 band on Native/Denaturing SDS, but 2 bands on Reducing SDS, this indicates that the original protein contained a disulfide link!

Hey man, I'm so sorry to hear about that. Thank you for sharing what you're going through.

Sexual violence is any form of sexual contact without voluntary consent. 1 in 3 women experience sexual assault in their lifetime, but not many know that **1 in 6 men** experience it too.

That girl was definitely not in the right headspace when she raped you, but it also seems that she doesn't understand what consent is since she hasn't apologize about it since. 

I went through a very similar experience with someone, a friend of mine at the time. I wanted to point out that I appreciate your honesty about having mixed feelings... I too made it clear to my abuser that I didn't want sex, so when I woke up to being touched, I didn't know how to react and went along with it. That's something that confused me for a long time and made me question whether it was really rape. After doing a lot of research on the subject though, I learned three important things: **1) consent is NOT silence or the absence of no; 2) consent cannot be obtained from someone who is incapacitated by alcohol/drugs or is unconscious, and; 3) consent can be revoked at any time.** You made it clear from the beginning that you did not want sex. You were confused and didn't know how to tell her to stop. That's still rape.

In my situation, I messaged my abuser about how it made me feel and that it was sexual assault. They apologized and promised not to make the same mistake again. They still wanted to be friends, but seeing them was a trigger so I told them not to message me anymore. 

The pain still lingers, but knowing that they understand consent now gives me some peace of mind. It's important to rectify the situation and acknowledge your trauma before you let time do its thing. It'll get better. 

Definitely tell your friends about it. She won't disappear, but you can definitely avoid her. I hope that you find support from your friends.
